explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM and human evaluations are conducted but LLM evaluates outputs using automated metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR etc.) while human annotators rate specific outputs (samples 11-15) on Likert scales, and no direct quantitative comparison or correlation between LLM and human judgments is reported

prompts.notes: Appendix F provides the LLMScore rubric emphasizing perspective, style, plot structure, and language variation; Appendix E provides the degeneration rubric with four equally weighted dimensions (syntactic integrity, semantic coherence, lexical sanity, noise symptoms)

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: indicates that all metrics achieved acceptable to excellent reliability

guidelines.notes: Appendix I contains detailed description of task definitions, instructions, and samples provided to annotators; human evaluation rated outputs on 5-point Likert scale for diversity, degeneration, and creativity

criteria_mapping.notes: LLMScore evaluates diversity while human evaluates diversity on Likert scale; LLM uses automated metrics for degeneration while human uses Likert scale for degeneration; creativity is only evaluated by humans
